minutes.headline: Finance Committee approved a letter to its state representative on school funding and named a backup for the budget task force.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the town manager's report, a first look at a 90-page financial policy manual, and a long debate over how to use the grant writing services money. It workshopped and approved a letter to the state representative ahead of a July 19 school funding meeting. It also discussed health insurance budgeting, consolidation of services and the budget calendar.

Chair asked for public comment at the end; none was offered.

budget_items.topic: Police mental health co-response clinician grant
budget_items.what_was_said: Police received a two-year grant shared with Lancaster, in addition to money from the opioid stabilization account.

budget_items.topic: Woodruff property hazardous materials cleanup bid
budget_items.what_was_said: The one bid came in well over the appropriation, so the town is trying to negotiate a change of scope.
Members disagreed over whether the grant writing services money should fund planning guidance or only writing specific grants. Proposals included an application process and an on-call bid list.
The letter says the formula gave a small increase and that a suggested correction would add state funding.
The letter gives school transportation spending for FY24 and FY25 and expects it to rise with a new contract.
The chair will reduce the letter's figures if circuit breaker reimbursement applies.
The town lost smart growth funding after eligible student counts dropped below the minimum.
The town pays the full health insurance bill and the school repays its share. Members debated a single line versus per-department lines.
Members discussed whether the finance committee can push back on the Monty Tech assessment.
A presentation on Chapter 90 and a yearly pavement management amount is wanted at a future meeting.

decisions.decision: Members agreed a survey of departments and an application process for grant writing help is the likely first step; the town manager will ask the procurement association about on-call grant services.
Chair will ask the DLS contact whether an organizational review can be requested, and by whom.
The letter will be edited (spell out SOA, soften the single-bid sentence, add DESE as a recipient, mention smart growth) before it goes to the select board and school committee.
Chair will try to schedule the Chapter 90 presentation for the July 25 meeting.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted unanimously by roll call to send a letter to its state representative on school funding.
The letter will be edited before it goes to the select board and school committee, with DESE added as a recipient.
The committee voted 6-0 by roll call to name a backup to the budget task force member.
Members split on whether grant writing services money should fund planning guidance or only specific grants, and reached no resolution.
Members debated a single health insurance line against per-department lines and reached no resolution.

why_it_matters: The letter puts the committee's case on state school aid and transportation costs on the record, which bears on how much of the school budget the town's tax bills must cover.
Whether health insurance appears as one line or several decides how clearly residents can see each department's share of that cost in the budget they vote on.
watch_next: A July 19 school funding meeting, which the letter was drafted ahead of.
A Chapter 90 and pavement management presentation, which the chair will try to schedule for the July 25 meeting.
